Home / What is OPC

What is an OPC?

A One-Person Company is China's newest company structure — designed for solo entrepreneurs who want full ownership with limited liability.

Understanding OPC

The Newest Way to Do Business in China

A One-Person Company (OPC / 一人公司) is a limited liability company with a single shareholder. Introduced as part of China's Company Law reforms, the OPC structure allows individual entrepreneurs — both Chinese nationals and foreigners — to register a company without needing a Chinese partner or a minimum capital requirement.

Six Key Features

What makes the OPC structure uniquely suited for solo entrepreneurs in China.

Single Owner

You are the sole shareholder. No partners, no joint decisions. You have full control over your company's direction and operations.

Limited Liability

Your personal assets are protected. Your liability is limited to your registered capital — a crucial safety net for entrepreneurs.

No Minimum Capital

Unlike WFOE structures, OPCs have no minimum registered capital requirement. Start with what you have and grow from there.

Full Foreign Ownership

Foreigners can own 100% of an OPC in designated areas like Suzhou Industrial Park. No Chinese partner is required.

Simple Structure

Less paperwork, fewer compliance requirements, and simpler reporting compared to larger corporate structures. Designed for efficiency.

Growth Pathway

OPC is a starting point, not a permanent state. As your business grows, you can add shareholders, convert to a larger structure, or attract investment.

Is OPC Right for You?

Who Qualifies?

The OPC structure is designed to be accessible. Here's who can register and what you'll need.

Who Can Register

Overseas Graduates — Recent graduates from foreign universities looking to start a business in China
Freelancers & Consultants — Independent professionals who need a legal business entity for their work
Solo Founders — Entrepreneurs with an innovative idea who want to test and validate their concept
Cross-Border Entrepreneurs — Business people who want a Chinese entity for market entry or trade
Chinese Nationals — Local entrepreneurs who prefer the simplicity of a one-person company structure
Remote Business Owners — People who want to establish a Chinese presence while managing operations flexibly

What You'll Need

1 Valid Passport — A current passport with sufficient validity for the registration period.
2 Proposed Company Name — Your preferred company name in both Chinese and English.
3 Business Scope Description — A clear description of your intended business activities.
4 Local Registered Address — A physical address in Suzhou Industrial Park (we can provide this).
5 Proof of Residential Address — Documentation of your current residential address from your home country.
6 Notarized Documents — Overseas documents may need notarization and authentication for use in China.
Busting OPC Myths

Common Myths Debunked

Don't let misconceptions hold you back from starting your business in China.

Myth

"Foreigners need a Chinese partner to open a company in China."

Reality: Foreigners can register a 100% foreign-owned OPC in designated areas like Suzhou Industrial Park. No Chinese partner is required.
Myth

"You need millions of RMB in registered capital to start."

Reality: OPCs have no minimum capital requirement. You can register with any amount you choose.
Myth

"OPCs are not real companies with legal standing."

Reality: OPCs are registered limited liability companies with the same legal standing as any other corporate entity in China.
Myth

"The registration process takes months to complete."

Reality: With our guidance, OPC registration typically takes only 15–20 working days from start to finish.
Side by Side

OPC vs Traditional Company vs WFOE

How the One-Person Company compares with other company structures for foreign entrepreneurs in China.

Feature OPC Traditional Company WFOE
Ownership 100% individual Multiple shareholders 100% foreign
Min Capital No minimum Varies Often high
Setup Time 15–20 days 1–2 months 2–3 months
Partners Required No Yes No
Foreign Ownership Yes (in SIP) No Yes (100%)
Can Invoice Yes Yes Yes
Can Hire Yes Yes Yes
Best For Solo entrepreneurs, early-stage startups Established local businesses Large foreign operations
